segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and all ate the same spiritual food,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they used to drink from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But with most of them God was not pleased, for they were laid low in the wilderness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now these things took place as examples for us, so that we would not be people who crave evil things, as they craved.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Do not become idolaters, as some of them were; as it is written,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to revel.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in a single day.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nor let us put Christ to the test, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the snakes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And do not grumble, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the destroyer.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now these things were happening to them by way of example, and they were written down as a warning for us, on whom the ends of the ages have come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So let anyone who thinks they are standing watch out that they do not fall.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No testing has overtaken you except what is common to humanity. But God is faithful: he will not let you be tested beyond what you are able, but with the testing he will also provide the way out, so that you are able to endure it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I speak as to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices sharers in the altar?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What am I saying, then? That food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No, but that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I do not want you to become sharers with demons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? We are not stronger than he is, are we?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: “All things are permitted,” but not all things are beneficial. “All things are permitted,” but not all things build up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let no one seek their own good, but the other person’s.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Eat everything sold in the market without raising any question on account of conscience,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “the earth is the Lord’s, and all that fills it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If one of the unbelievers invites you and you want to go, eat everything set before you without raising any question on account of conscience.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if someone says to you,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This has been offered in sacrifice,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: do not eat it, on account of the one who pointed it out and on account of conscience;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I mean not your own conscience but the other person’s. For why should my freedom be judged by someone else’s conscience?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If I partake with thanks, why am I denounced for something I give thanks for?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Give no cause for stumbling, whether to Jews or to Greeks or to the assembly of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: just as I also try to please everyone in everything, not seeking my own benefit but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

notes.phrase: a spiritual rock that followed them
notes.note: Water comes from a rock at both the start and the end of the wilderness journey (Exodus 17; Numbers 20). Jewish interpretive tradition, attested around Paul's time and later, concluded that the rock or well travelled with Israel. Paul appears to assume this tradition and identifies the rock with Christ.

The Greek word means a pattern or model, and the phrase can be read as 'examples for us' (warnings to learn from) or 'types of us' (events that prefigure the later community). Most translations take the first sense, which fits the warnings that follow. The second is possible and was influential in later Christian reading of the Old Testament.

The quotation is Exodus 32:6, describing the feast before the golden calf. The verb covers dancing, sport and festive merrymaking, here in a setting of idol worship. 'Play' now suggests children's games, so 'revel' is used. Many translations keep 'play'.

The reference is to the incident at Baal-Peor in Numbers 25, where the Hebrew and Greek texts both give twenty-four thousand dead. The reason for Paul's different figure is not known. Proposals include a slip of memory, a conflation with another census figure, or a count limited to a single day.

Manuscripts divide here between 'Christ', 'the Lord' and, in a few, 'God'. 'Christ' has early support and is the harder reading, since it has Israel in the wilderness testing Christ. Scribes are more likely to have softened it than to have created it, and it matches verse 4. The incident is the plague of snakes in Numbers 21.

The word occurs only here in the New Testament. It recalls the destroying agent of God's judgment in the exodus story (Exodus 12:23) and probably refers to the plagues that followed Israel's grumbling in Numbers 14 and 16. Readers would have understood an angel sent to carry out judgment.

The Greek noun and its verb cover both an enticement to sin and a trial that proves a person; English has to choose. 'Testing' is used because Paul has just used the related verb for Israel putting Christ to the test (verse 9) and the wilderness stories are stories of trial. 'Temptation' remains the more common rendering and is not wrong; the two senses overlap here.

The word means having a share in something together with others, or partnership. It is rendered 'sharing' here and its cognate 'sharers' in verses 18 and 20, so that the reader can see Paul using one word-family for the Lord's supper, Israel's altar and meals connected with idols. Older versions have 'communion'; many recent ones have 'participation'.

notes.traditional: what the Gentiles sacrifice / what pagans sacrifice
notes.note: Many manuscripts supply the subject 'the Gentiles'; the text translated here lacks it, and it is probably a scribal clarification. The sense is the same either way, since pagan worshippers are meant and not Israel from verse 18. The wording echoes Deuteronomy 32:17, 'they sacrificed to demons and not to God'.

Most scholars take these words, as at 6:12, to be a slogan current among the Corinthians, which Paul quotes and then qualifies; the quotation marks reflect that view. The Greek has no such marking, and the words could be Paul's own principle, restated with limits.

The word is a loan from Latin for a city's provisions market, where meat and other foods were sold. Some of the meat on sale had come from animals slaughtered in temple sacrifices. A buyer would not normally know which, and that is the question Paul says need not be asked.

The speaker uses the ordinary, respectful pagan term for meat from a temple sacrifice. It is not the disparaging Jewish and Christian term 'sacrificed to an idol' that Paul uses in verse 19. Whether the speaker is the pagan host, another guest or a fellow believer is not stated.

notes.phrase: why should my freedom be judged
notes.note: How these two questions fit the argument is disputed. They may give Paul's reason for the general rule of verses 25 to 27, that a believer's freedom is not really subject to another's scruples even when he abstains. They may instead voice an objection from the Corinthians, or explain why one should not invite condemnation by eating. In verse 30 'with thanks' could also be rendered 'by grace'.

The Greek word was the ordinary term for a civic gathering and, in the Greek Old Testament, for Israel assembled before God. 'Church' now suggests a building or institution, so this translation uses 'assembly' throughout. 'Church' is the near-universal rendering, and some object that 'assembly' sounds like a single meeting when an ongoing community is meant.

candidates.reason: The plural address to mixed congregations recurs in every letter, and translations vary between 'brothers', 'brothers and sisters' and 'friends'; it needs one policy.
It is rendered variously as fellowship, communion, participation, sharing and partnership across the New Testament, and the cognate κοινωνός should be visibly linked to it.
The choice between 'temptation' and 'testing' (with the verb πειράζω) recurs in the Gospels, James, Hebrews and the Lord's Prayer and should follow a stated rule.
The πορνεία word-group recurs widely and is rendered as fornication, sexual immorality or prostitution; readers should see one consistent choice.
It recurs in 1 Corinthians 8 to 10, Acts 15 and 21 and Revelation 2, with varying renderings (offered or sacrificed, food or meat, idol or idols) that should be fixed.
